facts.fact: The widow pension (IGNWPS) is Rs 300 a month at ages 40-79, per the NSAP About Us page
facts.quote: National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) – Widows aged 40 years and above. ₹300 per month (40–79 years) ₹500 per month (80 years and above)
facts.note: The Cabinet (PIB 14 Oct 2026, PRID 2323264) renamed IGNWPS as Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana and continued the widow pension 'in its existing form', so the amounts are unchanged.

facts.fact: It is Rs 500 a month from age 80, per the NSAP guidelines (Oct 2014)
facts.quote: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS): The eligible age is 40 years and the pension is Rs.300 per month. After attaining the age of 80 years, the beneficiary will get Rs.500/- per month.

facts.fact: The NSAP FAQ's Rs 200 a month for IGNWPS is outdated
facts.quote: The central contribution of pension under the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) is Rs. 200/- per month per beneficiary
facts.note: The quote shows the FAQ (Q18) still says Rs 200; 'outdated' is derived: the NSAP guidelines of Oct 2014 and the About Us page (last updated 28-10-2026) on the same site give Rs 300 (40-79) and Rs 500 (80+).

facts.fact: States add their own top-up to the central amount
facts.quote: 2.4.1 States are strongly urged to provide an additional amount at least an equivalent amount to the assistance provided by the Central Government so that the beneficiaries can get a decent level of assistance.

summary: Rs 300 (40-79) / Rs 500 (80+) confirmed on NSAP About Us and the 2014 guidelines; the NSAP FAQ Q18 still shows the outdated Rs 200; State top-up confirmed.
